Daniel
Karlberg

Game designer, producer and visual designer.

I’ve been making games since the late ’90s, starting with Quake II mods. Professionally I started in film and motion design, spent a decade launching games at Funcom, Klang and Unity, and now design them: economies, progression and the systems that keep players coming back. I work across the whole pipeline, from first prototype to the trailer and store page. I also hold an MA in Game and Interactive Media Design from Uppsala University, with a thesis on hybrid board games. Let’s talk →

2024 – now

Raketspel

Senior Technical Game Designer · Stockholm

I own design from concept to market test: economies, progression, levels and the documentation programmers build from. The studio publishes with partners including Voodoo and Homa.

What I did

  • Economy and progression design: currencies, sinks and sources, pacing curves modeled in spreadsheets.
  • Metagame systems for Radical Delivery: Global Radical Rank, Rads currency, collectibles, garage, mission-givers.

Lead designRΔY

RΔY

A calm puzzle-exploration game: tap anywhere to place the ray, drag back like a slingshot, and route the beam through the required number of mirrors before it reaches the goal crystal. No fail state — tension comes from finding the clever path, not from running out of shots. Levels descend through geological layers, from topsoil to deep earth.

Released
February 2026
Genre
Physics puzzle
Platforms
iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro
Languages
8, including Japanese, Korean and Chinese
Content
150+ levels across themed zones
Monetization
Rewarded hints and a one-time remove-ads purchase
Design pivot
Limited shots → unlimited attempts with bounce goals

My role

  • Owned the design from concept to launch and wrote the game design document.
  • Led the core pivot from a limited-shot beam to fire-anywhere, unlimited attempts with bounce objectives — removing the fail state and moving tension into the routing puzzle.
  • Designed slingshot aiming, minimum-bounce objectives, star ratings, and a three-tier hint system (firing point → angle → full path) that unlocks only after the player has struggled.
  • Built the difficulty and mechanic-introduction curve that orders 150+ levels into tutorial, easy, medium and hard tiers.
  • Designed the monetization: rewarded ads for hints, a one-time remove-ads purchase, and a photon soft currency — paying for help, never for progress.
  • Wrote a three-week production plan that turned playtest feedback (confusing mechanics, difficulty walls, no replay value) into a curated level progression, tutorial and star system.
  • Specified diegetic UI, the descend-into-the-earth transitions and audio feedback, like bounce pings that rise in pitch.

Project Røsvik

Project Røsvik

A first-person survival prototype. You’re a surveyor sent to Røsvik, an abandoned settlement in northern Norway once home to outcasts and pagan holdouts. Scavenge, craft from your backpack, unlock mystical powers and avoid mythological threats.

Status
Prototype / vertical slice
Genre
First-person survival
Role
Designer and product owner

My role

  • Led design direction, scope and implementation support.
  • Designed the two core powers (Thrum freeze, Eimr shockwave), the noise rules for stealth, and the diegetic watch, map and backpack inventory.
  • Drove a re-scope: backpack-only crafting, removed the timer, focused on two puzzle-heavy monuments.
  • Designed, set-dressed and lit the Boathouse; prototyped a grounded, bodycam-like player controller.
  • Recorded and implemented ambience, reverb zones and audio events.
  • Wrote most design docs, ran standups and planning.
